events.title: Edward the Confessor Dies, Leaving England Without a Clear Heir
events.description: King Edward the Confessor of England died childless. His death set off a fierce contest for the crown among several rival claimants.
events.significance: The succession crisis led directly to the Norman Conquest later that year. That conquest reshaped English language, law and society.

events.title: Battle of Nancy Ends the Reign of Charles the Bold
events.description: Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, was killed in battle outside the city of Nancy while fighting Lorraine and its Swiss allies.
events.significance: His death ended Burgundy's bid to remain an independent power between France and the Holy Roman Empire. Burgundy was absorbed into France.

events.title: Louis XV Survives an Assassination Attempt
events.description: Robert-François Damiens stabbed King Louis XV of France as he prepared to leave Versailles. The wound was not serious. Damiens was later executed in the traditional, brutal manner reserved for regicides.
events.significance: Damiens was the last person in France put to death by this method. The attack also showed how far the monarchy's popularity had fallen before the Revolution.

events.title: Ford Announces the Eight-Hour Day and $5 Wage
events.description: The Ford Motor Company announced an eight-hour workday and a minimum daily wage of $5, which was well above the typical factory pay of the era. Eligibility came with certain conditions.
events.significance: The move cut employee turnover and helped turn factory workers into customers. It became a landmark in modern labor and industrial history.

events.title: Alexander Dubček Rises to Power in Czechoslovakia
events.description: Alexander Dubček became leader of the Czechoslovak Communist Party and began pursuing a program of liberalizing reforms.
events.significance: His rise opened the period known as the Prague Spring, a reform movement that was ended by a Soviet-led invasion later that year.
